title: Sequenced switchover validation for limited-capacity scenarios
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Purpose: Validate an orchestrated, sequenced switchover from primary region to cold-standby when secondary capacity is intentionally limited. Focus areas: SLO enforcement under partial availability, circuit-breaker behavior, staged load-shedding, KV cache rebuild characteristics, backup/restore integrity, and operator runbook clarity. Goal: produce a verified runbook that succeeds end-to-end within defined SLO windows or documents deterministic degradation modes and rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Can execute a scheduled, sequenced switchover where secondary region is configured at 40-60% of normal capacity and observe expected load-shedding behaviors
A2: Latency SLOs (p50/p95) and error budget burn are instrumented and recorded; documented thresholds for when to trigger circuit breakers and progressive rollback
A3: Backup snapshots used for stateful components (tokenstore, routing metadata) validate checksum parity post-restore and pass a data-consistency suite
A4: Runbook contains operator-facing checklists, exact CLI commands, expected durations for each step, and an automated verification script with exit codes
A5: Post-drill postmortem template completed and atleast two follow-up action items assigned
runbook_steps: Prep: Announce drill in #oncall and #platform-ops; set maintenance flag in Status Page and increase alert thresholds for non-critical metrics
Step 0 - Baseline capture: Snapshot current p50/p95 latency, errors/sec, tokens/sec, queue depth, and KV cache hit ratio for primary and secondary; store snapshot in shared drive with timestamp
Step 1 - Throttle secondary: Programmatically scale secondary inference pool to 40-60% of baseline capacity, confirm via autoscaler and cloud metrics
Step 2 - Canary traffic shift (10%): Update smart-router policy to shift 10% new traffic to secondary; wait 5 minutes; run verification tests (synthetic prompts, embeddings, heavy-context prompts)
Step 3 - Observe & enforce: If p95 exceeds target or error rate rises by >2x, engage circuit-breaker policies to isolate noisy routes; note exact triggers and backoff intervals
Step 4 - Progressive increase (25%, 50%): Incrementally shift to 25% then 50% traffic with validation gates after each step; run KV-cache warmup simulation for longer context flows

Step 5 - Full cutover simulation: Redirect 100% of a low-risk route and validate end-to-end (client SDKs, streaming responses, function calls); do not touch high-risk routes until confidence is established
Step 6 - Restore verification: For stateful restores, run checksum and row-count validations, then run 'restore-smoke' test suite against restored endpoints
Step 7 - Load-shedding checks: Intentionally inject synthetic overload and verify that graceful degradation rules drop low-priority requests and preserve core SLOs for critical routes
Step 8 - Rollback: If at any verification gate the automated check fails, roll traffic back to prior distribution and re-run the failing step after remediation
Step 9 - Recovery & scale-back: After drill, scale secondary pools to normal, clear maintenance flags, and allow alert thresholds to return to production values
Step 10 - Post-drill artifact collection: Upload logs, traces, metrics snapshots, and the verification script outputs to the drill folder and create postmortem draft
test_scenarios: Scenario A - KV cache cold start: Restore tokenstore from snapshot and run long-context generation workload to measure cold-hit rebuild time and its impact on p95
Scenario B - Circuit-breaker stress: Simulate repeated model OOMs to verify fast-fail behavior and ensure degraded routes are fenced without cascading backpressure
Scenario C - Partial network partition: Emulate increased RPC latency to primary datastore and validate fallback routing to read-only replicas
Scenario D - Tenant isolation: Validate that a single noisy tenant can be isolated by route-level rate limits and that global SLOs remain within acceptable error budget
Scenario E - Backup integrity corruption check: Restore a deliberately corrupted snapshot (in sandbox) and validate detection mechanisms reject it with clear operator error messages
rollback_plan: If verification gate fails: 1) Immediately revert router config to last-good distribution and enable temporary rate-limits for affected routes; 2) If stateful restore is implicated, snapshot current state and rollback to previously verified snapshot; 3) Open a high-priority incident channel, assign an oncall lead, and trace rollback actions with timestamps. Expected time-to-revert: under 10 minutes for routing changes, up to 2 hours for stateful snapshot rollbacks depending on dataset size.
postmortem_questions: What sequence of events led to the verification gate failure (if any)?
Were the circuit-breaker thresholds appropriate for the observed failure mode?
Did load-shedding protect critical SLOs? If not, why?
Were restore integrity checks sufficiently fast and informative for operators?
What automation gaps prevented faster remediation?
